Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Solved correctly after 2 demo requests and 1 incorrect submission (the first output had wrong object placement/rows, not a useful rule; it was apparently rejected as not a valid ARC grid). Demos establish the rule.

## Transformation
Input contains a monochrome 1-shape and a 1xN or Nx1 ordered color palette strip containing distinct colors, with color 1 as one palette entry. Output preserves the grid dimensions and replaces the source shape with copies of its silhouette in every palette color, stacked vertically in the order of palette strip colors. The original color-1 copy stays at its original vertical position; other copies are placed contiguously above/below it so that total stack is centered/positioned to match demos. Remove palette strip. Preserve blank background.

More concretely, the test had an 18x15 grid: shape color1 at rows 6–8, cols 3–8 (0-index), silhouette:
row1: cols 5,6
row2: cols 4,7
row3: cols 3,4,5,6,7,8.
Palette strip at rows14–16, cols8–12 read vertically across rows as identical [2,3,1,8,7]. Correct output placed five shape copies in rows0–14, in palette order [2,3,1,8,7], each copy 3 rows tall, occupying the same cols 3–8. Rows15–17 blank. All else blank. Verified accepted.

## Demonstrations
Demo 1 (17x13): palette [4,1,6] appears as vertical columns at rows1–3; output renders silhouette in color4 at rows2–6, color1 at rows7–11, color6 at rows12–16. Strip removed. Shape silhouette is 6x7 at cols1–8; output copies preserve the silhouette and use one color per copy.
